answer.rationale: Three simultaneous pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing is tempting as a direct response to competitor pricing, but memory_73's record covers only a four-week window with standard reporting cadence and no visible long-term retention/LTV data — given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a competitor's price war risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that churn or erode margin, so I want to verify the original record before ever considering it, and even then treat it cautiously. Meanwhile, activation and onboarding completion are both down this quarter, and two independent archived memories (memory_31, memory_86) support that reducing friction in signup/onboarding produces durable activation gains — this is the more direct, lower-risk lever addressing an observed regression rather than reacting to a competitor's short-term tactic. I verify memory_31 to confirm the SMB signup-simplification result still holds since it's the oldest memory (day 12) underpinning this decision, and memory_73 to check whether promotional pricing's readout has any long-term revenue-quality signal before ruling it out this cycle. Given one experiment slot, I favor simplify_onboarding at standard scale: it targets two of the three live problems (activation and onboarding decline) with prior durable evidence, avoids the downstream value risk of a pricing race to the bottom, and preserves the option to run promotional pricing next cycle with better long-term-outcome data.
